description:
Factory AI GMO's commercial platform needs a durable, inspectable record of what the Software Construction Factory actually generated for a given Factory Run. `factoryRun` (tests/prd_factoryRun.json) deliberately stores only summary fields (`reviewPassed`, `reviewScoreSummary`, `gitBranchName`, `errorSummary`) and explicitly states it does NOT store full generated artifact bodies -- that gap is this module. Fifth module on the authenticated dependency chain (Account -> Organization -> Projects -> Factory Runs -> Artifacts -> Usage -> Billing), built by the same Software Construction Factory whose own output this module now has to hold.

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
- Each Factory Run can have zero or more Factory Artifacts attached, one per generation layer (database, backend, frontend) per review_fix_loop iteration.
- An artifact records which layer it is, its generated content (or a reference to it -- see Open Question #2), the reviewer's numeric score and pass/fail for that layer at that snapshot, and a compact issues summary.
- Authorized members can list artifacts for a Run (filtered by layer) and inspect one artifact's full content.
- This module does NOT execute the factory pipeline, does NOT push to GitHub, and does NOT store the raw LLM prompts or debate transcripts that produced the artifact -- only agent's structured output, the same boundary factoryRun itself draws around its own scope.

CONSTRAINTS -- already decided, satisfy them rather than re-deciding them
- A Factory Artifact is not a POS GMO retail-platform concept and must never be given a companyId -- it has no existing companyId relationship to POS GMO's own `companies` table, following the same tenant-independence reasoning already established for factoryAccount/organization/projects/factoryRun/pricingPlan.
- Content fields may contain customer PRD-derived code and, on a failed layer, error text; treat them as sensitive in logs the same way factoryRun treats prdSnapshot/errorSummary -- no plaintext content in application/error logs.
- created_At/updated_at remain server-controlled.
- This module reuses the SAME parent-reference pattern established across organization/projects/factoryRun: plain string reference field, not a formal FK, because factoryRun's own table is a validated design, not live yet.

OPEN ARCHITECTURAL QUESTIONS -- deliberately unresolved; do not silently pick an answer and hide the ambiguity
1. How does a Factory Artifact reference its parent Factory Run? This is a genuinely new gap this PRD surfaced, not inherited from an existing decision: organization and projects both have a human-chosen `slug` field designed specifically to be referenced externally before their table is live. factoryRun has NO such field -- its only identifier is `factoryRunId`, a DB-assigned autoincrement int that does not exist until the row is actually inserted into a live table. Until factoryRun's table is live, nothing can hold a stable, pre-assignment reference to a specific run the way `organizationSlug`/`projectSlug` do today. Whether factoryRun needs a client-generated correlation identifier (e.g. a UUID assigned at creation, independent of the DB PK) added to ITS OWN schema as a prerequisite, or whether factoryArtifact should simply wait until factoryRun is live and use a real `factoryRunId` FK at that point, is not decided here -- do not invent a UUID scheme on factoryRun's behalf as a side effect of this PRD.
2. Content storage shape: full text blob vs. a bounded/truncated preview vs. a hash + object-storage pointer. This is the exact same open question factoryRun's own `prdSnapshot` field left unresolved (Open Question #4 there), now facing it again for content that in practice runs much larger -- this session's own real runs produced frontend artifacts alone in the 17-25KB range per module, before combining database/backend/frontend together. Not decided here.
3. Retention: should artifacts be kept indefinitely, or pruned/archived after some period, particularly if full content blobs are what gets stored (see Question #2)? Not specified.
4. Relationship to reviewer's full issue detail: `review_result.issues` (as this session directly observed, e.g. pricingPlan's real run) can carry many entries with full messages, file names, and severities. Does `issuesSummary` stay a compact string, or does this module need a richer structured sub-record? Not decided here -- do not invent a nested issues table as a side effect of this PRD.
5. One artifact row per layer per Run (final state only), or one row per review_fix_loop iteration (showing what changed across up to 3 fixer attempts)? `iterationNumber` is included as a field either way, but whether earlier iterations are actually persisted or only the final one is an open design question for the Architect/Backend agents to decide and justify.
6. RESOLVED (was open): does this need its own top-level page, or is it purely nested content inside FactoryRunDetailPage? A real run first tried "nested, not standalone" and it produced a genuinely ambiguous result, not a clean answer -- frontend_agent generated a complete standalone page (full IonPage/IonContent scaffold) but left app_patches.menu_item/menu_section/icon_name/canAccess_key and setting_patch all null, because agents/frontend/prompt.py's App.tsx/Setting.tsx menu-registration section is unconditionally "MANDATORY, always include all 3 patches" with no way to express "this page intentionally has no menu entry." That's not a bug to patch -- it's this PRD's own open question causing exactly the ambiguous output an open question should cause. Resolved by reverting to this repository's established standalone-page pattern (every other module in this series) rather than teaching frontend_agent a new pattern it has never needed before. See docs/commercial-app-milestones.md Milestone 6.

This PRD intentionally leaves schema shape, relationships, and endpoints beyond standard CRUD to the Architect/Database/Backend agents to determine, consistent with the commercialization plan's instruction that the exact modules and schema should be discovered and designed by the Software Factory from the commercial requirements rather than assumed in advance.

fields.name: factoryRunRef
fields.description: Reference to the parent Factory Run. Deliberately a plain string placeholder, not a resolved identifier scheme -- see Open Architectural Question #1. Do not treat this field's shape as a settled decision.

fields.name: layer
fields.description: Which generation layer this artifact is: database, backend, or frontend.

fields.name: iterationNumber
fields.description: Which review_fix_loop iteration (1-3) produced this artifact snapshot. Whether all iterations or only the final one are actually persisted is Open Question #5.

fields.name: content
fields.description: The generated artifact body, or a reference to it. Exact storage shape (full blob vs. truncated preview vs. object-storage pointer + hash) is Open Question #2 -- not decided here. Sensitive: must not appear in logs in plaintext.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.description: SHA-256 hash of the full content, for integrity verification regardless of whether `content` itself is a full blob or only a pointer.

fields.name: layerScore
fields.description: Reviewer's numeric score (0-100) for this layer at this snapshot, mirroring review_result.scores[layer]. Null when the layer's construction agent never produced output (missing_artifacts case, not a score of zero -- see the reviewer's own artifact-presence invariant, agents/reviewer/rules.py).

fields.name: layerPassed
fields.description: Whether this layer individually met the pass threshold at this snapshot. Null has the same 'never reviewed' meaning as a null layerScore.

fields.name: issuesSummary
fields.description: Compact summary of reviewer issues for this layer at this snapshot. Whether the full structured issues[] array (message, file, severity per issue) needs its own representation is Open Question #4 -- not decided here.

fields.name: generatedByModel
fields.description: Which model produced this artifact, e.g. 'gemini-2.5-flash' -- for auditing the exact construction-layer reliability question Milestones 1-5 have so far only investigated manually by reading run logs.

frontend.uiPattern: List + Detail Layout -- standard standalone Admin page (Open Question #6 resolved: reverted to this repository's established pattern after a real run showed frontend_agent's App.tsx/Setting.tsx menu-registration path is unconditionally mandatory with no way to express a menu-less drill-down sub-page; see docs/commercial-app-milestones.md Milestone 6).

components.name: FactoryArtifactListStep
components.description: IonList grouped by layer (database/backend/frontend), each showing factoryRunRef, iterationNumber, layerScore/layerPassed badge, issuesSummary preview, search + IonSelect filters, paginated per existing list-view convention.

components.name: FactoryArtifactDetailPage
components.description: Full detail at /factory-artifacts/:id -- expand/collapse full content view (read-only, syntax-appropriate display), contentHash shown for integrity reference.

endpoints.description: Lists all artifacts for a given Factory Run reference, ordered by layer then iterationNumber. Restricted to Admin.
